question: Pascal said betting on God costs little and might win infinitely. What flaw did Diderot point out in one line?
answer: That an imam could reason the same way. The wager works for every religion that threatens infinite loss, and they cannot all be backed at once; each bet on one god risks the wrath of another. Diderot made the point in 1746. A wager with one table turns out to be a casino.
move: An argument that proves too many rival things proves none of them.
ask: Does my favourite argument for something work just as well for its rivals?
reference: Diderot, Pensées philosophiques, §59, in Œuvres philosophiques, ed. Vernière, Garnier, 1964
